units.translation: Turnebus restored θυοσκεῖς [you offer sacrifice] (a verb which Hesychius noted under the word θυοσκεῖν [to offer sacrifice]). θυοσκνεῖς [you offer sacrifice] in the first hand of M, corrected to θυοσκινεῖς [you offer sacrifice]. In Hesychius: θεοσκνεῖ: θεοὺς τιμᾷ [he serves the gods: he honors the gods].
By persuasion of what message do you offer sacrifice, sent around?
under the word θυοσκεῖν [to offer sacrifice]
he serves the gods: he honors the gods
Hear the knock at the courtyard door
οἱ θύραθεν [those from outside] is said of enemies encamped before the gates of the city
Knowing the affairs of those outside, you will be unharmed
But increase as much as possible the affairs of those outside
And I touched this man while being outside
Remember Orestes, even if he is outside
Indeed, I have no leisure to waste this outside time
Seeing the wealth outside, he groans
ὁ τοῦ ἐπαιτεῖν ἕνεκα κόπτων τὰς θύρας [the one who knocks on doors for the sake of begging].
Or am I a false prophet, a door-knocking babbler?
the one who knocks on doors for the sake of begging
And indeed no one of the doorkeepers would receive him with a cheerful mind
Thus H. L. Ahrensius for ἑκούσιον [voluntary]
Whenever the gods receive a sacrifice from their hands
From sacrifices a gentle hope appears
Of a sacrifice that stops the winds
Bringing courage from sacrifices to dying men
Alas, sacrifices before the towers of my father

Schol. τῆς παρὰ ταῖς θυσίαις γινομένης, ἀφ᾿ ἧς ἐνίοτε καὶ ἡ βάκχη. σημαίνει γὰρ καὶ τοῦτο καὶ τὴν καθαρὰν ἐσθῆτα, ὡς παρ᾿ Εὐριπίδῃ. ἢ, ἢ νενόμισται τοῖς Ἕλλησιν ἐν μάχαις · ἢ, ὡς νενομισμένον Ἕλλησι παρὰ τὰς θυσίας ὀλολύζειν. [Schol. of the one that occurs at sacrifices, from which sometimes also the Bacchic cry. For it signifies both this and the pure garment, as in Euripides. Or, or it is customary for the Greeks in battles; or, as it is customary for the Greeks to raise the ritual cry at sacrifices.]
A Greek custom of sacrificial cry

of the one that occurs at sacrifices, from which sometimes also the Bacchic cry. For it signifies both this and the pure garment, as in Euripides. Or, or it is customary for the Greeks in battles; or, as it is customary for the Greeks to raise the ritual cry at sacrifices
to perform sacred rites, to sacrifice
θύω [I rush] I am carried with raging impulse, I rage
which Triclinius explains by ὁρμῶσαν [rushing]: on which meaning see Thes. vol. 4 p. 469.
Wishing to offer a cake to the averting deities
They offered night-honored meals on the hearth of fire
It is necessary to sacrifice greatly and for the oracles to fall
It is necessary for the Argives to pray, to sacrifice, and to pour libations
Neither by sacrificing nor by pouring libations would you please
A wretched hare, mother of her own offspring, before the birth, to those sacrificing
And of her who was sacrificed pitilessly, of the same seed
And over the sacrificed one this song
